chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The servant is awakened three times during the night, so if he does not stand (for prayer), Satan comes to him and urinates in his ear.'
He said: 'And I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
They used to sleep but little in the night
He said: 'They missed very few nights, not standing (for prayer) in them.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of waking up three times for night prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the physical act of waking for Tahajjud to spiritual vigilance, using the vivid imagery of Satan urinating in the ear to signify deep, humiliating neglect of divine connection. He contextualizes Quran 51:17 by interpreting 'sleeping little' not merely as brevity of sleep, but as the consistency of those who rarely missed the night prayer, thereby elevating Tahajjud from a voluntary act to a hallmark of the righteous servants of Allah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al-Khazaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The servant wakes up three times at night, so if he does not stand (for Salāt), the Satanla comes to him and urinates in his ear’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[51:17] They used to sleep but little in the night.
Heasws said: ‘There were very few nights which they missed out on, not standing (for the Salāt) in them’.
en.sarwar: 18. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:
“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘A servant (of Allah) wakes up three times at night and if he still is not up (for Salah (prayer)) Satan comes and urinates in his ears.’
I then asked about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious,
‘They would sleep very little at night’.
[51:18] The Imam replied, ‘There were few nights in which they would miss getting up for Salah (prayer)).”’
